descriptionChirho: The Hebrew noun פַּחַת (pachat) denoting a pit, hole, or snare dug in the ground, used both literally for physical pits and figuratively for danger or calamity. All four clusters represent grammatical inflections of the same meaning: with article (eng: the pit, spa: la fosa/el hoyo, arb: الْحُفْرَةِ, kor: 구덩이/함정의, swa: shimo), with conjunction (eng: and pit, spa: y fosa, arb: وَحُفْرَةٌ, hin: और गड्ढा), plural (eng: the pits, spa: las cuevas, arb: الْحُفَرِ, kor: 구덩이들, swa: mashimo), and indefinite singular (eng: a pit, spa: precipicio, arb: الْهُوَّةِ, hin: खड्ड). The consistent translation across languages confirms a single semantic sense.
